title: Randy's Smothered Pork Chops
imageAlt: Smothered pork chop with mushroom gravy, rice, and vegetables
summary: Bone-in chops with mushrooms, onions, and gravy. Next time: one-hour bake, creamier gravy, and mashed potatoes.
ingredients: 4 bone-in center loin pork chops, about 1 inch thick
1 large yellow onion, sliced into ¼-inch half-moons
½ cup whole milk or half-and-half
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. While it heats, season the pork chops with salt and black pepper on both sides.

Get a skillet hot over medium-high heat with a little butter or oil. Brown the chops for 2–3 minutes per side. You're building flavor here, not cooking them through, so pull them once they've got good color.
Move the chops out of the skillet. Add the onions and give them 2–3 minutes to soften, then add the mushrooms and cook another 4–5 minutes. Don't clean the skillet—we want all those browned bits.
Stir in the cream of mushroom soup, onion soup mix, beef broth, milk, and Worcestershire. Scrape the bottom of the skillet as you stir so all that pork-and-onion goodness ends up in the gravy.
Put the chops in a baking dish and pour the gravy, mushrooms, and onions over everything. Cover the dish tightly with foil so the chops stay moist.
Bake for 1 hour, then check them. The first batch went 1 hour 15 minutes and got a little dry near the bone, so don't automatically give them extra time. Add only 5–10 minutes if they truly need it.
Let the chops rest for about 5 minutes. Serve them over mashed potatoes and don't be stingy with the mushroom gravy.

journal.general: The first attempt baked for 1 hour 15 minutes and was slightly dry and tough near the bone; the outer meat was perfect. Keep the generous mushrooms and onions. There was plenty of gravy.

title: Mississippi Pot Roast
imageAlt: Mississippi pot roast served over mashed potatoes with pepperoncinis
summary: Rich, tangy chuck roast served over creamy mashed potatoes with plenty of pepperoncinis.
steps: If you've got the time, pull the roast from the refrigerator 20–30 minutes before cooking. If you don't, the world won't end—just move on.
Pat the roast dry and season it lightly with black pepper. Skip the extra salt; the ranch and au jus packets bring plenty of their own.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the roast for 2–3 minutes per side, including the edges, until you've got a good dark-brown crust. We're browning it, not cooking it.
Move the roast into the slow cooker. Sprinkle the ranch seasoning and au jus mix evenly over the top, then park the whole stick of butter right on top.
Scatter 10–15 pepperoncinis around the roast and pour in 2–4 tablespoons of the pepperoncini juice. More pepperoncinis is not a mistake—we learned that on the first cook.
Cover and cook on LOW. Start checking around 6 hours, but let the roast tell you when it's done. A fork should slide in easily and twist the meat apart without a fight.
If you're getting hungry and the roast is still stubborn, switch the slow cooker to HIGH and give it another 45–60 minutes. Don't pull it just because the clock says dinner—the tough parts need time.
When every section is tender, pull or shred the meat and stir it back through those cooking juices. Save every damn drop; that's where a lot of the flavor lives.
Pile it over mashed potatoes with plenty of juice and some sliced pepperoncinis on top.

journal.general: ★★★★★ Randy Favorite. The first test used a 2.47 lb chuck roast. Cook to tenderness rather than strictly by the clock: if a fork can lift the roast without pulling it apart, it needs more time. The center became tender before the thicker outer portions, so continue cooking until all sections pull apart easily. The flavor was spot on. Next time use more pepperoncinis, add sliced pepperoncinis to each serving, and save every drop of the cooking juices for gravy and reheating leftover mashed potatoes. Served with mashed potatoes boiled exactly 18 minutes and finished with a hand mixer.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: Flavor was outstanding. The center became tender first, while the thicker outer portions needed more time. Use more pepperoncinis next time and add sliced pepperoncinis when serving.

title: Randy's Simple Mashed Potatoes
summary: Simple, creamy mashed potatoes with butter, warm milk, and sour cream.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salt for the cooking water, plus more to taste
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 2-inch chunks. They don't need to be perfect; reasonably even pieces just help them finish at the same time.
Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover them with cold water, and add about 1 tablespoon of salt. Starting cold lets the centers cook before the outsides turn to mush.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook for about 18–20 minutes. Start checking at 18—the potatoes are ready when a fork slides in easily without resistance.
Drain them well, then put them back in the hot pot over low heat for about a minute. This cooks off some leftover water so we get creamy potatoes instead of watery ones.
Add the butter first, then the warm milk and sour cream. Warm milk matters here; dumping refrigerator-cold milk into hot potatoes doesn't do anybody any favors.
Mash by hand or use the hand mixer just until they're smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Then stop. Seriously. Once they're smooth, quit beating them or you'll turn perfectly good mashed potatoes into potato glue.

journal.general: Made to serve under Mississippi Pot Roast or smothered pork chops. Excellent fresh and reheats well with a splash of milk. Even better with leftover pot roast juices or homemade gravy.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note:
Boiled exactly 18 minutes.
Butter first.
Warm milk.
Hand mixer.
Excellent.

title: Breakfast Sliders
summary: Hawaiian rolls layered with scrambled eggs, ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach, then baked until golden.
ingredients: 12 dinner rolls or Hawaiian sweet rolls
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Slice the whole slab of rolls horizontally so you end up with one big top and one big bottom—don't separate the individual rolls yet.
Set the bottom slab in a 9×13-inch baking dish. Spread the scrambled eggs evenly over it, then layer on the ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach.
Put the top slab of rolls back on. Brush it generously with melted butter and finish with a little black pepper.

Bake for about 20 minutes, until the tops are golden and the cheese is properly melted. If the cheese still looks stubborn, give it another couple minutes rather than serving cold cheese in the middle.
Let the sliders sit for a minute or two, then cut along the roll seams into 12 sandwiches. Serve them warm before everybody starts stealing the crispy corner pieces.

journal.general: La Jefa requested these again, so they are automatically a favorite. Adapted from Tasty's Breakfast Sliders recipe. Take our own photo next time and record any changes Randy and Lisa prefer.

title: Randy's Camp Breakfast Tacos
imageAlt: Camp breakfast taco on a paper plate beside a Coleman stove, with a lightly charred tortilla
summary: Built at home, finished over the campfire. Crispy tortilla, bacon, eggs, cheese, and plenty of picante.
steps: At home, cook the bacon until crisp, drain it, and chop it into bite-size pieces. Crispy matters because it'll soften a little when we reheat it at camp.
Scramble the eggs in butter until they're just barely set, then season lightly with salt and pepper. Don't cook the hell out of them now—they're getting heated again tomorrow.
Let the bacon and eggs cool for about 10 minutes before building the tacos. Wrapping everything while it's steaming is a good way to make soggy tortillas.
Divide the eggs, bacon, and cheddar among the four tortillas. Roll them tightly, folding the ends in as you go so breakfast doesn't fall into the fire.
Wrap each one individually in heavy-duty foil and refrigerate overnight. A little parchment inside the foil or a very light coating of oil can help keep the tortilla from sticking.
At camp, use indirect heat over campfire embers or a grill whenever you can. That's the easy way to warm the center without cremating the tortilla.

If the Coleman stove is the only option, put the foil-wrapped tacos in a skillet or on a griddle over the LOWEST flame. Do not put them directly over the burner—we tried that, and it turned breakfast into charcoal.
Turn them every 2–3 minutes and start checking around 8–10 minutes. They're done when the centers are hot and the cheese has melted; they don't earn bonus points for staying on the heat longer.
Open the foil carefully, add plenty of picante sauce, and eat them while they're hot. The picante is not optional.

journal.general: Designed for camping. Assemble everything at home so breakfast at camp is almost effortless. Let the eggs cool slightly before rolling so the tortillas stay firm. Heavy-duty foil works best. Picante sauce isn't optional—it gets added after opening the foil at camp.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: Coleman stove was way too hot. Tortillas burned and stuck to the foil before the centers warmed through. Next time use a skillet or griddle over the lowest flame and turn every 2–3 minutes. Lightly grease the foil or use parchment inside the foil.

title: Slow Cooker Carnitas
imageAlt: Turkey taco topped with avocado, cilantro, cotija cheese, and salsa verde, with crispy carnitas in the background
summary: Tender, flavorful slow-cooked pork finished under the broiler for crisp, browned edges.
ingredients: 1 boneless pork roast, 4–5 lb, excess fat trimmed and cut into 3-inch chunks
1 tablespoon chipotle powder, or 1 chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, minced
steps: Put the pork, beer or chicken stock, onion, garlic, chipotle, cumin, black pepper, chili powder, and salt in the slow cooker. Give everything a good stir so the seasoning isn't sitting in one sad pile on top.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6–8 hours or HIGH for 4–5 hours. Ignore the clock if the pork is still fighting you—it isn't done until a fork goes in easily and the meat practically falls apart.
When the pork is tender, crank the broiler to HIGH and line two big baking sheets with foil. Leave the cooking juices in the slow cooker. We absolutely want those later.
Shred the pork into bite-size pieces and move it to the baking sheets with a slotted spoon. Spread it into a single layer so the edges can actually see the broiler.
Broil the first sheet for about 5 minutes, watching for browned, crispy edges. Broilers have no sense of humor, so keep an eye on it.
Pull the pan out, spoon about ¼ cup of the reserved cooking juices over the pork, and toss it around. That gives us crispy edges without drying out the meat.
Broil it for about 5 minutes more, then hit it with another ¼ cup of those juices. Repeat the same crisp-and-juice routine with the second pan.
Serve immediately in tacos, burritos, quesadillas, salads, nachos, or bowls. And save the leftover cooking liquid—it is way too good to pour down the drain.

journal.general: Adapted from Gimme Some Oven. The pork does not need to be seared before slow cooking because it is crisped under the broiler at the end. Save the cooking juices and add them back after each broiling step so the carnitas stay juicy. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months.

shopping: Chipotle powder or chipotle pepper in adobo sauce
Tortillas and desired toppings for serving

title: Turkey, Bacon & Avocado Sammie
imageAlt: Toasted turkey sandwich layered with melted pepper jack, crispy bacon, and avocado
summary: A hot turkey sandwich with melted pepper jack, crispy bacon, and cool avocado on toasted bread.
ingredients: About 1/2 avocado, mashed, or prepared guacamole
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Cook the bacon until it's properly crisp, then drain it on paper towels. Limp bacon has no business on this sandwich.
Pile the turkey onto one slice of bread and cover it with the pepper jack. Leave the other slice plain for now.
Put both bread halves in the toaster oven open-faced. Toast until the bread is golden and the pepper jack is completely melted over the turkey.
Spread the mashed avocado or guacamole over the plain toasted slice. Add a little salt and black pepper if it needs it.
Lay the crispy bacon over the melted cheese, close the sandwich, and press it together gently.
Eat it immediately while the bread and bacon are still crisp, the cheese is hot, and the avocado is cool. That's the whole damn point.

journal.general: Toast the sandwich open-faced so the bread gets crisp while the pepper jack melts. Add the bacon and avocado after heating so the bacon stays crisp and the avocado stays cool.

title: Creamy Italian Sausage & Potato Soup
imageAlt: Creamy Italian sausage and potato soup with spinach
summary: Creamy potato soup with sweet Italian sausage, Parmesan, and spinach. Lisa loved it; next time Randy wants less sausage.
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into bite-size pieces
3 sweet Italian sausage links, casings removed
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
2 generous handfuls fresh spinach or chopped kale
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste
½ teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
1 tablespoon butter or olive oil, only if needed for sautéing
steps: Heat a Dutch oven or soup pot over medium-high heat. Pull the sausage from the casings and brown it for 6–8 minutes, breaking it into bite-size chunks as it cooks. Three links is enough—we tried five, and the sausage took over the whole damn soup.
Move the browned sausage to a plate, but leave 1–2 tablespoons of the rendered fat behind. If the pot somehow looks dry, add a little butter or olive oil.
Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, until it's soft and starting to brown. Add the garlic for the last 30–60 seconds; garlic burns fast, so don't wander off.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for about a minute. Add the Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes, and black pepper and let the spices wake up in the hot pot.
Slowly pour in the chicken broth while stirring and scraping the bottom. Those browned sausage-and-onion bits belong in the soup, not glued to the Dutch oven.
Add the potatoes, bring everything to a gentle boil, then back it down to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 12–15 minutes, until a fork slides easily into the potatoes.
Return the sausage and any juices on the plate to the pot. Turn the heat to LOW and stir in the milk.
Warm the soup gently for 5–7 minutes. Don't let it rip into a hard boil after the milk goes in. Stir in the Parmesan and let it melt into the broth.
Add the spinach and give it 2–3 minutes to wilt. If you're using kale instead, give it more like 4–5 minutes so you're not chewing your soup.
Now taste it before reaching for the salt. The sausage, broth, and Parmesan have already brought plenty to the party. Adjust the salt, black pepper, and red pepper only if it actually needs them.
Ladle it into bowls and finish with Parmesan and plenty of freshly cracked black pepper. For a thicker soup, mash a few potato chunks against the side of the pot and stir them back in.

journal.general: First cook: used 5 sausage links instead of the recommended 3. Randy thought the sausage overpowered the soup and use 3 links next time. Lisa said, ‘It’s delicious.’ Keep this in the Maybe category for Randy, but it is La Jefa Approved. For a thicker soup, mash several potato chunks against the side of the pot near the end and stir them back in. For a brothier soup, add another ½–1 cup chicken broth. Reheat gently over medium-low heat with a splash of milk if needed.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: First cook. Used 5 sausage links. Too much sausage for me—the sausage was overpowering. Next time use 3 links. Lisa said, ‘It’s delicious.’ Maybe make again with less sausage.

title: Green Chile Chicken Enchilada Casserole
summary: Layered corn tortillas, green chile chicken, roasted poblano, Monterey Jack, crema, and Cotija. Built to freeze and reheat well.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked shredded chicken (about 1½ lb raw chicken, or meat from 1 rotisserie chicken)
1 small yellow or white onion, diced
1 can (15 oz) green enchilada sauce or about 2 cups salsa verde
¼–½ teaspoon crushed red pepper or chipotle powder, optional
1½ cups shredded Monterey Jack or Oaxaca cheese
½ cup Mexican crema or sour cream, plus more for serving
½ cup crumbled Cotija cheese, plus more for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Roast the poblano for 10–15 minutes, turning it until the skin is blistered and charred in spots. Cover it in a bowl for 5–10 minutes, then peel off the loose skin, remove the stem and seeds, and dice it. Turn the oven down to 375°F for the casserole.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until it's soft, then add the garlic for another 30–60 seconds. Don't brown the garlic—we're making enchiladas, not garlic chips.

Add the shredded chicken, poblano, green chiles, cumin, Mexican oregano, black pepper, and optional red pepper or chipotle. Stir in about ¾ cup green enchilada sauce and ¼ cup sour cream. Give it 2–3 minutes to get hot, then taste it before adding salt. Cotija is coming later and that stuff brings plenty.
Spread just enough green enchilada sauce over the bottom of an 8×8- or 9×9-inch baking dish to keep the first tortilla layer from drying out.

Tear or cut tortillas to cover the bottom. Add half the chicken mixture, about one-third of the Monterey Jack, and a light drizzle or a few small dollops of sour cream. It doesn't have to look pretty; we're burying it under another layer.
Build the second layer the same way: tortillas, the rest of the chicken, another third of the Monterey Jack, and a little more sour cream.
Finish with one last tortilla layer. Pour the remaining green sauce over the top, then cover it with the rest of the Monterey Jack and about ½ cup Cotija.

Cover loosely with foil and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes. Pull the foil and give it another 10–15 minutes, until the edges are bubbling and the cheese on top is melted and starting to look irresistible.

Let it sit for 10 minutes before cutting. Yes, actually wait—the layers need a chance to settle unless you want enchilada landslide on the plate. Finish with cilantro, extra Cotija, lime, sour cream, and sliced jalapeño if you want the heat.

For leftovers, cool the casserole and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Portion it once cold and freeze individual servings in airtight containers. Thaw overnight when you can and reheat covered; a spoonful of salsa verde will wake it right back up if it seems dry.

journal.general: First test planned for 2026-08-25. Randy already has Cotija to use. Keep the Cotija as a salty finishing cheese rather than the main melting cheese; Monterey Jack or Oaxaca provides the melted layers. Intended as a freezer-friendly casserole. Add cook notes and a photo after dinner.

shopping: Cooked shredded chicken or rotisserie chicken
Green enchilada sauce or salsa verde
